title: Pissta: Monte-Carlo-Labeled Random Timing DAG Datasets for Physics-Informed Surrogate SSTA (pissta-2k/5k/10k + OOD-100)
description:
Datasets of random single-source/single-sink timing DAGs (6–14 gates, 1–4 reconvergence points, 2D spatial coordinates, per-gate loads) with Monte-Carlo-labeled critical-path delay statistics (mean/std; N=10,000 samples, seed 42 per graph) under correlated process variation (inter-die + spatial + Pelgrom mismatch), produced by the Pissta physics-informed SSTA framework. Each graph ships MC labels, per-gate linearized delay sensitivities, per-gate var_d/load_ff², and an analytical-SSTA (iterative Clark MAX) baseline.

Versions: pissta-2k (2,000 graphs; paper-exact Stage 6A dataset used for all reported Stage 6B/6C/7/8 results; frozen artifact), pissta-5k and pissta-10k (companion scaling releases; graphs 000000–001999 are byte-identical entries of pissta-2k, so 2k ⊂ 5k ⊂ 10k), and pissta-ood100 (100 out-of-distribution topologies, 15–25 gates, ≥2 reconvergences; Stage 7 evaluation set).

Reproducibility: MC labels, graph structures, and stratified splits recompute bit-exactly from the released code and seeds; file SHA256s and process constants are pinned in per-dataset manifest.json. The pissta-2k gate-load value→gate pairing is frozen (the 2026-08 build drew loads in Python set-iteration order); load values are bit-exact. Extension graphs use a canonical, process-independent pairing. Regeneration: zenodo/scripts/generate_pissta.py; verification: zenodo/scripts/verify_release.py.

Disclaimers: all model parameters (α=1.3, Vdd=1.0 V, L_nom=45 nm, W_nom=90 nm, Vth_nom=0.40 V) are deliberately simple demonstration parameters for software/methodology validation — not silicon-calibrated, and not real technology results. Labels are Monte-Carlo emulations from the repository's own variation sampler, not measurements or SPICE simulations of a physical process.

Licensing: code MIT; data CC-BY-4.0. Recommended: separate deposits per dataset (CC-BY-4.0) plus one code deposit (MIT), linked via related identifiers.
